findings.problem: Only the residual half of the manager's open question, recorded because it was asked: bare مقام is also this catalogue's word for "location" (7 values, e.g. ui.agents.skills.detail.location_label = "مقام", ui.canvas.create_file_dialog.location = "مقام", ui.chat.highlights.file_resolution_failed = "...اس کا مقام..."), and in general Urdu the word carries a third sense, standing/rank, which the audio sibling removes with its پلے بیک qualifier. In this string the risk does not materialise: {label} کا binds مقام to the clip, the element is role="slider" with aria-valuetext time text (sound-player.tsx:501-510), and the sibling audio seek slider already ships the same word (ui.chat.attachments.playback_position = "پلے بیک کا مقام"). So the revision is unambiguous enough and gates nothing; the note exists so a later wave knows the qualifier was considered, not missed.
findings.recommendation: Keep "{label} کا مقام". Optional, only if a future wave wants the maximal explicit reading: "{label} میں پلے بیک کا مقام" (the prior ur-sol auditor's alternative) — rejected here because it imports پلے بیک, a word the English "{label} position" does not carry, while its sibling's English "Playback position" does.

per_key_checks.assessment: Accuracy: preserved — the English names the playback position of one clip; {label} کا مقام says exactly that, with no addition, omission or polarity change, and nothing destructive or permission-bearing is affected (it is an aria-label on a seek slider, sound-player.tsx:455 applied to a role="slider" at :501-510). Grammar: the revision fixes the agreement the previous value carried by construction rather than by error — پوزیشن is feminine so کی was right there, مقام is masculine so کا is right here; either way the genitive sits on the fixed noun and never on the inserted title, so an arbitrary user-supplied clip title (Latin, mixed script, spaces, punctuation, an already-genitive Urdu phrase) leaves the construction grammatical. The shape "{placeholder} کا X" ships 25 times in the ur catalogue (e.g. ui.common.actions.date_time_picker.choose_time = "{label} کا وقت منتخب کریں", ui.chat.tags.rename_label = "{name} کا نام بدلیں"), and {label}-initial order matches this key's own siblings ({label} چلائیں, {label} کو وقفہ دیں). Terminology: it now uses the catalogue's existing word for the same control concept, ui.chat.attachments.playback_position = "پلے بیک کا مقام", which is the whole point of the prior MINOR, and پوزیشن drops to 0 occurrences in the whole ur catalogue (was 1, this key). Register: terse neutral noun phrase, no address, no imperative; مقام is not an over-Persianised import here — it is the catalogue's settled word and appears in 11 values across 8 files. Punctuation/script: Urdu script only, no trailing punctuation, no invisible or bidi control characters, placeholder Latin-brace bytes intact. Fit: 15 characters, no maxCells declared for this key. The English sidecar's stated intent ("Names playback position for this specific clip, not a play/pause action... retain the clip label... Translate only the surrounding word for position") is met exactly: the source has no "playback" qualifier and the translation adds none.

open_question_assessment.question: Is مقام, which also means 'location' elsewhere in the ur catalogue, unambiguous enough for a seek-slider name next to ui.chat.attachments.playback_position = "پلے بیک کا مقام"?
open_question_assessment.answer: Yes, unambiguous enough; no change requested.
reasoning: The word never stands alone: {label} کا binds مقام to the clip, and the element it names is role="slider" with aria-valuetext carrying the time (sound-player.tsx:501-510), so a screen reader announces name + role + value together; the 'location' and 'standing/rank' readings have no purchase in that frame.

The catalogue already spends مقام on this exact control concept: ui.chat.attachments.playback_position = "پلے بیک کا مقام" labels the other audio seek slider (audio-attachment.tsx:189). Two audio sliders in one product now use one word, which is the AT-facing consistency the prior round asked for.
The two strings differ in the source too — "Playback position" carries پلے بیک in Urdu, "{label} position" does not — so the remaining asymmetry mirrors the English instead of contradicting it.

Measured correction to the prior round's evidence, offered so the ledger does not inherit a soft number: the earlier receipt argued from '64 occurrences in 24 ur files', but that is the substring count — of the 65 substring hits today, 52 are مقامی (local), 2 are مقامات (places) and 11 are the bare word (10 before this revision). The word is still settled for the position sense (playback_position plus 'مقام پر' in ui.projects and ui.shell), but on 4 position-sense values rather than 64 — the sibling audio label, not the raw count, is what carries this decision.
open_question_assessment.residual_risk: A reader who meets the string with no musical context could parse 'X کا مقام' as X's place/standing; that is what N1 records. It does not gate.

The note 'Two clips may be present together, so retain the clip label' is consistent with the component receiving a per-clip `label` prop. The declared placeholder contract ('insert verbatim... Word order may change around {label}') is honoured by the value.
